definition: the rubric I ran on the marriage, and the one dimension I refused a veto

settled:
Each of us decided we were ready to commit in a non-standard way. For Jen it was realising that how concerned she was about hurting my feelings with her decision was itself evidence of how much she cared.

I evaluated the relationship against a rubric, the way I do all important decisions. It scored high on every dimension except physical attractiveness, which was medium.

A line kept running through my head about never making a pretty woman your wife. I do not know where it is from, but it stuck. I decided I did not want to be the kind of person who lets physical attractiveness hold a veto over choosing an eternal companion. External beauty is temporary and the least important thing about a person, so I moved forward.

Looking back I can tell I was feeling the infatuation crush. That datum matters: the crush and infatuation system does work normally in me, against the flat affect everywhere else. The decision was still made on reason rather than on the crush.

title: How I Decided To Marry Her
